content: 1. Constipation-related adverse reactions: Eluxadoline can increase the risk of serious constipation-related adverse effects. Avoid co-administration with other drugs that cause constipation. Monitor patients closely. 2. Diphenhydramine and eluxadoline: These drugs may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or consider alternative therapies. 3. Eluxadoline and eluxadoline metabolism: Eluxadoline increases dipyridamole levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Eluxadoline and BCRP substrates: Eluxadoline may increase systemic exposure to co-administered BCRP substrates. Monitor closely. 5. Eluxadoline and disopyramide: Eluxadoline increases disopyramide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. CYP3A substrates with narrow therapeutic indices: Exercise caution when co-administering eluxadoline with CYP3A substrates that have a narrow therapeutic index. Monitor closely. 7. Eluxadoline and doxorubicin: Eluxadoline increases doxorubicin levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Duloxetine and eluxadoline: Duloxetine increases eluxadoline levels by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 9. Strong CYP1A2 inhibitors: Due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism, use caution when co-administering with strong CYP1A2 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 10. Duvelisib and eluxadoline: Eluxadoline increases duvelisib levels. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with BCRP transport inhibitors may further increase duvelisib levels. 11. Eltrombopag and eluxadoline: Eltrombopag increases eluxadoline levels by reducing its metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administered with OATP1B1 inhibitors, reduce the eluxadoline dose to 75 mg PO BID. 12. Enasidenib and eluxadoline: Enasidenib increases eluxadoline levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid co-administration with sensitive OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP substrates. If unavoidable, adjust substrate dosages and monitor closely. 13. Encorafenib and eluxadoline: Encorafenib increases eluxadoline levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Encorafenib, an OATP1B1 inhibitor, may increase the concentration and toxicities of OATP1B1 substrates. 14. Eluxadoline and epoprostenol: Eluxadoline increases epoprostenol levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Eluxadoline and ergotamine: Eluxadoline increases ergotamine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Erythromycin and eluxadoline: Erythromycin increases eluxadoline levels by reducing its metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administered with OATP1B1 inhibitors, reduce the eluxadoline dose to 75 mg PO BID. 17. Everolimus and eluxadoline: Eluxadoline increases everolimus levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Fentanyl and eluxadoline: These drugs may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid co-administration with other drugs that cause constipation. 19. Fluconazole and eluxadoline: Fluconazole increases eluxadoline levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Fluorouracil and eluxadoline: Fluorouracil increases eluxadoline levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Fluoxetine and eluxadoline: Fluoxetine increases eluxadoline levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Flurbiprofen and eluxadoline: Flurbiprofen increases eluxadoline levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Fluvoxamine and eluxadoline: Fluvoxamine increases eluxadoline levels by affecting CYP2C19 and CYP1A2 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 24. Fostemsavir and eluxadoline: Fostemsavir inhibits OATP1B1/3 transporters, potentially increasing eluxadoline levels. Avoid co-administration or modify the dose of OATP1B1/3 substrates. Monitor closely. 25. Gemfibrozil and eluxadoline: Gemfibrozil increases eluxadoline levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administered with OATP1B1 inhibitors, reduce the eluxadoline dose to 75 mg PO BID. 26. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir and eluxadoline: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may decrease the therapeutic effects of eluxadoline, while eluxadoline may increase plasma levels of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir. Monitor closely. 27. Glyburide and eluxadoline: Glyburide increases eluxadoline levels by reducing its metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administered with OATP1B1 inhibitors, reduce the eluxadoline dose to 75 mg PO BID. 28. Hydromorphone and eluxadoline: These drugs may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid co-administration with other drugs that cause constipation. 29. Hydroxyzine and eluxadoline: These drugs may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Avoid co-administration with other drugs that cause constipation. 30. Ibuprofen and eluxadoline: Ibuprofen increases eluxadoline levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Iloprost and eluxadoline: Eluxadoline increases iloprost levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Imatinib and eluxadoline: Eluxadoline increases imatinib levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Indinavir and eluxadoline: Indinavir increases eluxadoline levels by reducing its metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administered with OATP1B1 inhibitors, reduce the eluxadoline dose to 75 mg PO BID. 34. Indomethacin and eluxadoline: Indomethacin increases eluxadoline levels by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Itraconazole and eluxadoline: Itraconazole increases eluxadoline levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38.
